main_text.l: stus. Tandem concinnatum corpus omni-
busq; suis partibus absolutum intelligen-
te formatur anima, qua tunc est, & dicitur
homo. Quoniam autem in procreatione ho-
minis plurium animarum succefsio statui-
tur, idcirco quæruntnonnulli, an ipsæ ani-
mæ huiusmodi sint, ut quæ uegetans est nō
decedat, sed à sentiente cōtineatur: Et hæc
ab intelligente: an uel sentientis accefsu ue-
getans abeat, & intelligentis aduentu ab-
olearur sentiens? Quòd si prior admittatur
quæstio, in uno & eodem homine tres si-
mul erunt animæ, uegetans, sentiens, & ra-
tionalis: quòd sane non solùm absurdum,
sed & plane ridiculum est. Sic enim unus
& idem homo erit plura, nempe & homo,
& brutum, atq; planta. Si uero posterior ue-
ra sit, ter morietur fœtus, terq; renascetur.
Primùm enim deleta uegetante interibit,
& sentientis aduentu regenerabitur: qua
rursum sublata, miser ille peribit: tertioque
in postremæ animæ aduetu, qua homo est,
morietur. Vt autem hæc diluatur ambigua,
dicendum est aduentu intelligetis animæ,
quæ secum omnem adducit animanti per-
fectionem, præcedentes adesse non ut for-
mas essentiales, sed ut facultates, ac pote-
states,

page.notes: Long s rendered as s; Greek none. Catchword absent. Page is a faithful layout with the "D 4" signature at the foot. The scan is slightly faded; the word "states," at the line-end after the signature was taken as "states,", and the first-line fragment "stus." stays a fragment. Some words in the lower half were read with [?] where uncertain: "states," and the middle words of "uegetans" were read with care. Corrections needed in the first lines: "statuitur" and "decedat" are clear; "contineatur" is printed "cotineatur" and is transcribed as printed. Note that the transcription above is not final; check the printed lines "uero posterior uera sit" against the scan, as the scan reads "posterior ue ra fit".
